title: Edge GPU ops scratchpad
content:
Daily scratchpad — quick brain dump for GPU/capacity/networking work

03/13/2026 morning check
- Quick status: 6/8 edge nodes online in us-west-2a, all dedicated instances up. One node (edge-eu-03) pending reboot from kernel update.
- Current cluster GPU inventory (approx): total gpus: 48 (A100x16:8, A10x6:24, T4x8:16). Allocated: 38. Spare capacity: ~10 GPUs but fragmentation across zones.

Priority TODOs
- [ ] Defrag allocation across zones before Friday deploy window (action: schedule mini-shift with autoscaler).
- [ ] Run quantization sanity tests on cuda-12 images (PR#834) — measure latency delta and mem usage. Target: <=5% latency regression.
- [ ] Validate NVLink health on edge-a100-02 (reported elevated memory errors yesterday). Follow checklist in runbook.
- [ ] Network egress test for new VPC peering to partner region (ping/iperf to 10.12.5.1). Add to canary route.

Notes / quick commands
- How to force drain a node without killing GPU jobs: kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=600
- Check GPU processes: sudo nvidia-smi topo --matrix; docker exec -it <container> nvidia-smi; htop + nvtop on host.
- Clear cache between runs: sudo sh -c 'echo 3 >/proc/sys/vm/drop_caches' (only for dev nodes)

Recent observations
- 03/11: noticed ~20% increase in p99 generation latency during sustained batches — traced to inter-node network jitter on us-west-2b. Suspect NIC offload mismatch after kernel upgrade.
  * Action taken: rolled kernel back on 3 nodes, opened INFRA-421. Awaiting vendor driver backport.

Capacity planning notes
- Next 30d expected onboarding: two mid-size customers likely to request Dedicated capacity of ~12 A10 GPUs each. If both convert, need +24 GPUs by mid-April.
- Short-term options: burst policy to use spot A100s (costy) or reallocate fraction of A10 pool from internal teams. Talk to sales to get commitment date.
- Cost flag: A100 spot prices vary a lot; set budget alert at $X/day for bursts (see billing/alerts).

Networking reminders
- Revisit MTU across peered VPCs — mismatch observed causing fragmentation; ask net infra to standardize MTU=9001 on all transit gateways.
- Re-run iperf test after peering change: iperf3 -c 10.12.5.1 -P 8 -t 60. Record jitter/pkt-loss.

Troubleshooting checklist (for GPU memory errors)
- Check dmesg for GPU/PCIe events.
- Run nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total,utilization.gpu --format=csv -l 5 for 1 minute.
- If ECC errors: escalate to hardware support, capture lspci -vvv and smart logs.

Mini action plan for today
- 0900-0930: sync with Leah — final plan for zone defrag. Confirm autoscaler adjustment steps.
- 1000-1200: run quantization bench on staging with new cuda image (PR#834). Save perf logs to /tmp/quant-bench/ethan-20260313.log and upload to confluence test page.
- 1400: reach out to net-infra for MTU rollout schedule (cc: Samir).
- 1600: short postmortem notes for yesterday's kernel rollback and update INFRA-421 with timelines.

Reminders to self
- When scheduling maintenance, send short note to #prod-notify with explicit fallback times and contact (pager) for 30min after windows start.
- Keep one spare A10 in cold pool for emergency Dedicated trials — confirm with finance how to account for it.

Loose ideas / experiments
- Try lightweight local KV caching for small prompt prefixes at edge to reduce repeated token workloads (prototype on T4s). Expect >15% token reduction on chat echoes.
- Evaluate cheaper quant routes: 4-bit int8-like path for smaller models on A10s — run quality eval with existing prompt-set (eval-rl-2026).

Open questions
- Can we automate node defrag without customer impact? (risk: rolling allocations might cause slight thrash)
- What is lead time from sales for Dedicated commits? Need concrete date to plan procurement.

Quick links
- INFRA-421: https://jira.redwood.internal/browse/INFRA-421
- PR#834: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/834
- Runbook: confluence://runbooks/gpu-infra

End of today
- Log any anomalies into runbook and tag with date. Keep this file as my short-term memory for ops tasks.

-- Ethan
